To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the plasma-lyph exchange and interstitial tissue distribution volumes of charged proteins are determined by the interaction of the proteins with fixed negative charges in the interstitial space of the lung.
plasma-lymph clearance and extravascular distribution volumes are affected by the charge of macromolecules.
the initial clearance of cationic lactate dehydroganase 5 (LDH 5) across the capillary endothelium was significantly higher than that of anionic LDH in the dog lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the plasma-lyymph exchange, initial clearance, and extravascular distribution volumes in lung of two isozymes of lactate dehydroganase with different isoelectric points.
the interstitial distribution volumes and the initial clearances of two isozymes of lactate dehydroginase (LDH).
the transport of macromolecules in pulmonary lymph and the extravascular distribution of these macromolecules in lung tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plasma-lyph exchange of cationic macronolecules in the lung is retarded by the ionic interactions between the positively charged cationic macrorolecules and the fixed negative charges located on the endothelial cells, the basement membrane, and the interstitial matrix of the lung.

the extravascular distribution of LDH 4.2 is dependent upon the charge and the molecular weight of the macromolecule, and is influenced by the plasma-lynh exchange and the interstitial distribution volume of the macromolecules.
, in the lung, the plasma-lyph transport and interstitial distribution of cationic and anionic macromolecules are regulated by different mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma proteins of different charges have different rates of clearance from plasma, distribution volumes in lung tissue and lymph, and different lymph/plasma ratios.
the plasma-lyph exchange of cationic and anionic macromolecules in lung is influenced by their charge, molecular size, and extravascular distribution volumes.

the initial clearance of charged macromolecule from the capillary is dependent on their molecular charge, the extravascular tissue distribution volume of charged macromolecular is dependent on their size and charge, and their interstitial tissue distribution volume is dependent on their charge and size and the fixed negative charge density of the tissue matrix.
